_generated: Authored prose input to the WebSocket protocol manifest. The generator (just ws-manifest) merges these descriptions with topic validation metadata from the Rust registry and binary layouts from the compiled codecs. Topic names, wire layouts, config bounds, cadences, control gates, keys, backpressure classes, capabilities, the event vocabulary, and the clock-stamped message list must be edited in Rust.

frames.description: LED color data for subscribed zones.

spectrum.description: Audio FFT spectrum and beat data.

events.description: Discrete daemon and render lifecycle events.

frame_events.description: Raw per-frame render timing events for diagnostics.

screen_zones.description: Ambilight zone grid extracted from screen capture: smoothed, color-tuned per-sector RGB colors plus letterbox state.

zone_preview.description: Per-zone preview frame stream. config.zones names the zones to deliver, or ["all"]; the daemon does preview work only for zones some subscriber selects.

sensors.description: Latest host CPU, GPU, memory, and component sensor snapshot.

display_preview.description: Per-display JPEG preview frame stream, keyed by device.

interactive_preview.description: Interactive scene preview lane keyed by a client-chosen preview id. Subscribing opens the lane; unsubscribing closes it.

input_events.description: Host input events (key and pointer edges) for automation clients. Control-authorized subscription only; never part of the default events relay.

clock.contract: Every server message listed in stamped_messages carries two publication stamps at the top level. timestamp is wall-clock time (ISO 8601 UTC, millisecond precision) and follows the host clock through NTP slews and manual steps. mono_us is microseconds on the daemon's monotonic clock: it never moves backwards and does not jump when the wall clock is stepped, so order messages, measure intervals, and judge frame pacing with it. Its rate is not guaranteed steady (on Linux it follows NTP frequency corrections), so a long session repeats round-trip calibration rather than assuming a fixed rate. An event is stamped when it is published on the daemon bus, before any relay queueing, so frame_rendered stamps follow the render thread rather than socket delivery. Snapshot messages (metrics, device_metrics, sensors) are stamped when the daemon assembles them. The hello names the clock: clock_epoch is an opaque identity for this daemon run's monotonic origin, compared by equality only, and mono_us is the clock's reading when the daemon built the hello, which lets a client estimate the offset to its own monotonic clock. Every message listed in round_trip_messages carries mono_us alone: a command response reads the clock after the command finishes and immediately before the daemon hands the response to the socket, so a client that sent the command at its own monotonic time t0 and received the response at t1 knows t0 - mono_us <= offset <= t1 - mono_us, where offset is client time minus daemon time. mono_us values are comparable only within one clock_epoch, and a restarted daemon announces a new one. Events from different producers are stamped independently and can arrive out of stamp order with no fixed bound, and a resync notice is stamped when it is built, so it can precede retained events with older stamps; sort by mono_us when order matters.
